questions.q:
Let $f(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin 3 x & 1 & 2\left(\cos \frac{3 x}{2}+\sin \frac{3 x}{2}\right)^2 \\ \cos 3 x & -1 & 2\left(\cos ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}-\sin ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}\right) \\ \tan 3 x & 4 & 1+2 \tan 3 x\end{array}\right|$
Then, the value of $f^{\prime}(x)$ at $x=(2 n+1) \pi, n \in I$ (the set of integers) is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,
$f(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin 3 x & 1 & 2\left(\cos \frac{3 x}{2}+\sin \frac{3 x}{2}\right)^2 \\ \cos 3 x & -1 & 2\left(\cos ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}-\sin ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}\right) \\ \tan 3 x & 4 & 1+2 \tan 3 x\end{array}\right|f^{\prime}(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\frac{d}{d x}(\sin 3 x) & 1 & 2\left(\cos \frac{3 x}{2}+\sin \frac{3 x}{2}\right)^2 \\ \frac{d}{d x}(\cos 3 x) & -1 & 2\left(\cos ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}-\sin ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}\right) \\ \frac{d}{d x}(\tan 3 x) & 4 & 1+2 \tan 3 x\end{array}\right|+\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin 3 x & \frac{d}{d x}(1) & 2\left(\cos \frac{3 x}{2}+\sin \frac{3 x}{2}\right)^2 \\ \cos 3 x & \frac{d}{d x}(-1) & 2\left(\cos ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}-\sin ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}\right) \\ \tan 3 x & \frac{d}{d x}(4) & 1+2 \tan 3 x\end{array}\right|+\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin 3 x & 1 & 2 \frac{d}{d x}\left(\cos \frac{3 x}{2}+\sin \frac{3 x}{2}\right)^2 \\ \cos 3 x & -1 & 2 \frac{d}{d x}\left(\cos ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}-\sin ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}\right) \\ \tan 3 x & 4 & \frac{d}{d x}(1+2 \tan 3 x)\end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}3 \cos 3 x & 1 & 2\left(\cos \frac{3 x}{2}+\sin \frac{3 x}{2}\right)^2 \\ 3 \sin 3 x & -1 & 2\left(\cos ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}-\sin ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}\right) \\ 3 \sec ^2 3 x & 4 & 1+2 \tan 3 x\end{array}\right|+\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin 3 x & 0 & 2\left(\cos \frac{3 x}{2}+\sin \frac{3 x}{2}\right)^2 \\ \cos 3 x & 0 & 2\left(\cos ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}-\sin ^2 \frac{3 x}{2}\right) \\ \tan 3 x & 0 & 1+2 \tan 3 x\end{array}\right|+\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin 3 x & 1 & 2 \times 2\left(\cos \frac{3 x}{2}+\sin \frac{3 x}{2}\right) \\ \cos 3 x & -1 & 2\left(-2 \cos \frac{3 x}{2} \times \frac{3}{2} \sin \frac{3 x}{2}\right. \\ & & \left.-2 \sin \frac{3 x}{2} \times \frac{3}{2} \cos \frac{3 x}{2}\right) \\ \tan 3 x & 4 & \left(0+2 \times 3 \sec ^2 3 x\right)\end{array}\right|$
At $x=(2 n+1) \pi$,
$f^{\prime}(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}3(-1) & 1 & 2(1) \\ 0 & -1 & 2(-1) \\ 3 & 4 & 1+0\end{array}\right|+0+\left|\begin{array}{ccc}0 & 1 & 4(0-1) \times\left[-\frac{3}{2}(-1)+\frac{3}{2} \times 0\right. \\ -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0\end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}-3 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{array}\right|+0+\left|\begin{array}{ccc}0 & 1 & -6 \\ -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0\end{array}\right|\begin{aligned}=[-3(-1+8)-1(0+6) & +2(0+3)] \\ & +[0-1(0-0)-6(-4)]\end{aligned}=-21+24=3$

questions.q: Derivative of $x^x$ is
questions.solution:
Let $y=x^x$
Taking log on both sides, we get $\log y=x \log x$
On differentiating w.r.t. x , we get $\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x} & =\frac{x}{x}+\log x \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x} & =y(1+\log x)=x^x(1+\log x) \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $u=x^2+y^2$ and $x=s+3 t, y=2 s-t$, then $\frac{d^2 u}{d s^2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given that, u=x^2+y^2 and $\quad x=s+3 t, y=2 s-t$ Now, $\quad u=x^2+y^2\begin{aligned} & =(s+3 t)^2+(2 s-t)^2 \\ & =s^2+9 t^2+6 s t+4 s^2+t^2-4 s t \\ \Rightarrow \quad u & =5 s^2+2 s t+10 t^2\end{aligned}$ On differentiating with respect to $s$, we get $\frac{d u}{d s}=10 s+2 t$
Again differentiating $\frac{d^2 u}{d s^2}=10$

questions.q: A real valued differentiable function $f$ satisfies $f(x)+f(y)+2 x y=f(x+y) \forall x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. Given $f^n(0)=0$, then value of $\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} f(\sin x) d x$ will be
questions.solution:
$f(x)+f(y)+2 x y=f(x+y)...(i)$
differentiating the equation,
$\Rightarrow f^{\prime}(y)+2 x=f^{\prime}(x+y)$
at $y=0f^{\prime}(0)+2 x=f^{\prime}(x)\Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=2 x$
Integrating both sides.
$\int f^{\prime}(x)=\int 2 x \cdot d x\Rightarrow f(x)=x^2\therefore I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} f(\sin x) d x\Rightarrow I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \sin ^2 x \cdot d x...(ii)\Rightarrow I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \sin ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right) d x=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos ^2 x \cdot d x \ldots(iii)$
Adding Eqs. (ii) and (iii)
$2l=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right) d x=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} 1 \cdot d x\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & 2l=\frac{\pi}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & l=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{array}$

questions.q: The derivative of $\tan ^{-1}   \left(\frac{\sqrt{1+x²}-1}{x}\right)with respect to $\tan ^{-1}$\left(\frac{2 x \sqrt{1-x^2}}{1-2 x^2}\right)$at $x=0$, is
questions.solution:
Let $y=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+x^2}-1}{x}\right)$
Putting $x=\tan \theta$, we get
$\begin{aligned} y & =\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sec \theta-1}{\tan \theta}\right)=\tan ^{-1}\left(\tan \frac{\theta}{2}\right) \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1} x\end{aligned}$
On differentiating both sides w.r.t. x , we get
$\begin{array}{r}\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{1}{2\left(1+x^2\right)} \\ \text{ and } z=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x \sqrt{1-x^2}}{1-2 x^2}\right)\end{array}$
Putting $x=\sin \theta$, we get
$\begin{aligned} & \quad z=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 \sin \theta \cos \theta}{\cos 2 \theta}\right)=\tan ^{-1}(\tan 2 \theta) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad z=2 \theta=2 \sin ^{-1} x\end{aligned}$
On differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\frac{d z}{d x}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$
Thus, $\frac{d y}{d z}=\frac{d y / d x}{d z / d x}=\frac{1}{4\left(1+x^2\right)} \sqrt{1-x^2}$
$\therefore \quad\left[\frac{d y}{d z}\right]_{x=0}=\frac{1}{4}$

questions.q: If $2^x+2^y=2^{x+y}$, then $\frac{d y}{d x}$ is equal to
questions.solution:

$2^x+2^y=2^{x+y}$
On differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$, we get
$2^x \log 2+2^y \log 2 \frac{d y}{d x}=2^{x+y} \log 2\left(1+\frac{d y}{d x}\right)\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad\left(2^y-2^{x+y}\right) \frac{d y}{d x}=2^{x+y}-2^x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{2^x\left(2^y-1\right)}{2^y\left(1-2^x\right)}=2^{x-y}\left(\frac{2^y-1}{1-2^x}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $y=|\sin x|^{|x|}$, then the value of $\frac{d y}{d x}$ at $x=\frac{-\pi}{6}$ is
questions.solution:
Given $y=|\sin x|^{|x|}$ In the neighbourhood of $-\frac{\pi}{6},|x| and |\sin x|$ both are negative i.e., $y=(-\sin x)^{-x}$
Taking log on both sides, we get $\log y=-x \log (-\sin x)\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}= & (-x) \frac{1}{-\sin x}(-\cos x)+\log (-\sin x)(-1) \\ & =-x \cdot \cot x-\log (-\sin x) \\ & =-[x \cot x+\log (-\sin x)]\end{aligned} \\ & \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x} & =-y[x \cot x+\log (-\sin x)]\end{aligned} \\ & \begin{aligned} \therefore\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{x=-\frac{\pi}{6}}=\frac{2^{-\frac{\pi}{6}}}{}[6 \log 2-\sqrt{3} \pi]\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x^2-y^2}{x^2+y^2}\right)=\log a$, then $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}$ equals
questions.solution:
We have $\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x^2-y^2}{x^2+y^2}\right)=\log a\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x^2-y^2}{x^2+y^2}=\sin (\log a)\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1-\tan ^2 \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta}=\sin (\log a)$ (on putting $y=x \tan \theta$.) $\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & \cos 2 \theta & =\sin (\log a) \\ \Rightarrow & & 2 \theta & =\cos ^{-1}(\sin \log a) \\ \Rightarrow & & \theta & =\frac{1}{2} \cos ^{-1}\{\sin (\log a)\}\end{aligned}\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \cos ^{-1}\{\sin \log a\}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{1+\frac{y^2}{x^2}} \cdot \frac{x \frac{d y}{d x}-y}{x^2}=0\Rightarrow \quad x \frac{d y}{d x}-y=0\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y}{x}$ ....(i) $\Rightarrow \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\frac{-y}{x^2}+\frac{1}{x} \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-y}{x^2}+\frac{1}{x}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) ; \quad\{$ from $(i)\}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=\frac{-y}{x^2}+\frac{y}{x^2}=0$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f$ be twice differentiable function satisfying $f(1)=1, f(2)=4, f(3)=9$, then
options: there exists atleast one $x \in(1,3)$ such that $f^{\prime \prime}(x)=2$
questions.solution:
Let $g(x)=f(x)-x^2\Rightarrow g(x)$ has atleast 3 real roots which are $x=1,2,3$ (by mean value theorem)
$\Rightarrow g^{\prime}(x)$ has atleast 2 real roots in $x \in(1,3)\Rightarrow g^{\prime \prime}(x)$ has atleast 1 real root in $x \in(1,3)\Rightarrow f^{\prime \prime}(x)=2$ for atleast one $x \in(1,3)$

questions.q: The motion of a particle along a straight line is described by the function $x=(2 t-3)^2$, where $x$ is in metre and $t$ is in second. Then, the velocity of the particle at origin is
questions.solution:
Given that, $x=(2 t-3)^2$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\frac{d x}{d t}=2(2 t-3)(2)$
At origin, $x=0\begin{array}{lc}
\therefore & 2 t-3=0 \Rightarrow t=\frac{3}{2} \\
\therefore & \text{ Velocity }=\frac{d x}{d t}=4\left(2 \times \frac{3}{2}-3\right)=0
\end{array}$

questions.q: If $Z=f(x+a y)+\phi(x-a y)$, then
questions.solution:
Given that,
$\begin{aligned} Z & =f(x+a y)+\phi(x-a y) \\ Z_x & =f^{\prime}(x+a y)+\phi(x-a y) \\ \Rightarrow \quad Z_{x x} & =f^{\prime \prime}(x+a y)+\phi^{\prime \prime}(x-a y)\end{aligned}$ and $\quad Z_y=a f^{\prime}(x+a y)-a \phi^{\prime}(x-a y)\Rightarrow \quad z_{y y}=a^2 f^{\prime \prime}(x+a y)-a^2 \phi^{\prime}(x-a y)$
Hence, $a^2 Z_{x x}=Z_{y y}$

questions.q: If $f(x)=|x|^{|\sin x|}$, then $f^{\prime}\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Since, $f(x)=|x|^{\sin x}$ when $x \lt 0 \begin{aligned} f(x) & =(-x)^{(-\sin x)} \\ & =e^{-\sin x \log (-x)} \\ \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x) & =e^{-\sin x \log (-x)}\end{aligned} \left(-\cos x \log (-x)-\frac{\sin x}{x}\right) \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=(-x)^{-\sin x}(-\cos x \cdot \log (-x)-\frac{\sin x}{x})$
$\Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{1 / \sqrt{2}}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \log \frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{4}{\pi}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right) \begin{aligned} & \quad \\ & =\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{1 / \sqrt{2}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \log \frac{4}{\pi}-\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{\pi}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $f(x)=\log _x(\log x)$, then $f^{\prime}(x)$ at $x=e$ is
questions.solution: We have, $f(x)=\log _x(\log x)=\frac{\log (\log x)}{\log x}\Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{\log x \cdot \frac{1}{\log x} \cdot \frac{1}{x}-\log (\log x) \cdot \frac{1}{x}}{(\log x)^2}=\frac{1-\log (\log x)}{x(\log x)^2}\therefore \quad f^{\prime}(e)=\frac{1-\log (\log e)}{e(\log e)^2}=\frac{1}{e}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The functions $u=e^x \sin x$ and $v=e^x \cos x$ satisfy the equation
questions.solution:
We have, $u=e^x \sin x$ and $v=e^x \cos x$ On differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\frac{d u}{d x}=e^x \sin x+e^x \cos x=u+v$
and $\frac{d v}{d x}=e^x \cos x-e^x \sin x=v-u\therefore v \frac{d u}{d x}-u \frac{d v}{d x}=v(u+v)-u(v-u)=u^2+v^2$
Now, $\quad \frac{d^2 u}{d x^2}=\frac{d u}{d x}+\frac{d v}{d x}=u+v+v-u=2 v$
and $\quad \frac{d^2 v}{d x^2}=\frac{d v}{d x}-\frac{d u}{d x}=(v-u)-(v+u)=-2 u$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x)=(a x+b) \sin x+(c x+d) \cos x$, then the values of $a, b, c$ and $d$ such that $f^{\prime}(x)=x \cos x$ for all $x$, are
questions.solution:
We have, $f(x)=(a x+b) \sin x+(c x+d) \cos x\begin{aligned}
f^{\prime}(x)=a \sin x+(a x+b) \cos x & +c \cos x -(c x+d) \sin x
\end{aligned}$
But $f^{\prime}(x)=x \cos x$ for all $x$ (given)
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore x \cos x=(a-d) \\
& \quad \sin x+(b+c) \cos x+a x \cos x-c x \sin x
\end{aligned}$
Equating the coefficients of $\sin x, \cos x, x \cos x and x \sin x$, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \quad a-d=0, b+c=0, a=1, c=0 \\
& \therefore b=c=0 \text{$ and $} a=d=1
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a particle is moving such that the velocity aćquired is proportional to the square root of - the distance covered, then its acceleration is
questions.solution:
Let $v$ be the velocity of the particle when the distance covered is $s$. Then,
$v \propto \sqrt{s}$ (given)
$\Rightarrow \quad v=\lambda \sqrt{s}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d v}{d x}=\frac{\lambda}{2 \sqrt{s}}\Rightarrow \quad v \frac{d v}{d s}=\frac{\lambda \nu}{2 \sqrt{s}}=\frac{\lambda^2}{2}=$ constant
$\therefore$ The acceleration is constant

questions.q: If $z=\tan (y+a x)+\sqrt{y-a x}$, then $z_{x x}-a^2 z_{y y}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have, $z=\tan (y+a x)+\sqrt{y-a x}\Rightarrow z_x=a \sec ^2(y+a x)+\frac{(-a)}{2 \sqrt{y-a x}}\Rightarrow z_{x x}=2 a^2 \sec ^2(y+a x) \tan (y+a x)-\frac{a^2}{4}(y-a x)^{-3 / 2}$ and $z_y=\sec ^2(y+a x)+\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{y-a x}}\Rightarrow z_{y y}=2 \sec ^2(y+a x) \tan (y+a x)-\frac{1}{4}(y-a x)^{-3 / 2}\begin{aligned} & a^2 z_{y y}=2 a^2 \sec ^2(y+a x) \cdot \tan (y+a x) -\frac{a^2}{4}(y-a x)^{-3 / 2}\end{aligned}$
Now, $z_{x x}-a^2 z_{y y}=0$

questions.q: If $f_n(x)=e^{f_{(n-1)}(x)}$, for all $n \in N$ and $f_0(x)=x$, then $\frac{d}{d x}\left\{f_n(x)\right\}$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\frac{d}{d x}\left\{f_n(x)\right\}=\frac{d}{d x}\left\{e^{f_{n-1}(x)}\right\}=e^{f_{n-1}(x)} \frac{d}{d x}\left\{f_{n-1}(x)\right\}=f_n(x) \cdot \frac{d}{d x}\left\{e^{f_{n-1}(x)}\right\}=f_n(x) \cdot e^{f_{n-2}(x)} \cdot \frac{d}{d x}\left\{f_{n-2}(x)\right\}=f_n(x) \cdot f_{n-1}(x) \ldots f_2(x) \frac{d}{d x}\left\{f_1(x)\right\}=f_n(x) \cdot f_{n-1}(x) \ldots f_2(x) \cdot f_1(x) \cdot \frac{d}{d x} e^{f_0(x)}=f_n(x) \cdot f_{n-1}(x) \ldots f_2(x) \cdot f_1(x) \cdot \frac{d}{d x}\left(f_0(x)\right)=f_n(x) \cdot f_{n-1}(x) \ldots f_2(x) \cdot f_1(x) \cdot \frac{d}{d x}(x)\quad \quad\left[\because f_0(x)=x \text{ (given) }\right]=f_n(x) \cdot f_{n-1}(x) \ldots f_2(x) \cdot f_1(x).$

questions.q: If $y=\sqrt{(a-x)(x-b)}-(a-b) \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{a-x}{x-b}}$, then $\frac{d y}{d x}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $x=a \cos ^2 \theta+b \sin ^2 \theta\therefore \quad a-x=a-a \cos ^2 \theta-b \sin ^2 \theta=(a-b) \sin ^2 \theta$
and $x-b=a \cos ^2 \theta-b \sin ^2 \theta-b=(a-b) \cos ^2 \theta\therefore \quad y=(a-b) \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta-(a-b) \tan ^{-1} \tan \theta\therefore \quad y=(a-b) \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta-(a-b) \tan ^{-1} \tan \theta=\frac{a-b}{2} \sin 2 \theta-(a-b) \theta\therefore \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d y / d \theta}{d x / d \theta}=\frac{(a-b) \cos 2 \theta-(a-b)}{(b-a) \sin 2 \theta}=\frac{1-\cos 2 \theta}{\sin \theta}=\tan \theta=\sqrt{\frac{a-x}{x-b}}$
